pr.title: refactor(server): resolve project and worktree folders in one place
pr.body: ## What changed - New shared `KnownWorkspaces` service (`apps/server/src/workspace/KnownWorkspaces.ts`) decides which folders a client-named `cwd` may act in: a T3-managed worktree folder (current and previous settings), a registered project, or the worktree a non-deleted thread is bound to. `ReviewService` and `projects.writeFile` both use it, and it replaces the folder checks that used to live inside `ReviewService`. - File saves (`projects.writeFile`): - refuse a `cwd` outside every known project or worktree folder. - resolve the deepest existing part of the target to its real path and require the result to stay inside the project's real root, so a symlink cannot send a save outside the project. Dangling symlinks are refused, and the file is opened without following a final symlink. - never land in git's own folders: any `.git` path segment (Windows spellings included), or a folder git reads as a repository, such as `.bare` or a bare `repo.git`. `.gitignore`, `.github/` and similar files still save. - keep a file name that contains a backslash as one file on macOS and Linux. - Refusals reuse the existing `resolved_path_outside_root` / `workspace_path_outside_root` failures, so clients need no changes. - New worktrees always go in the managed worktrees folder: - `t3_worktree_handoff` no longer accepts `path`. - The `vcs.createWorktree` request only accepts `path: null`. The key stays because older servers require it. - The default location uses the resolved `cwd`, so the folder is always named after the repository. - Turn start only recreates a missing worktree at `//`, compared by real path. ## Behavior changes - Saves are refused in a worktree no thread is bound to, in a `cwd` that does not exist (main used to create it), inside `.git`, and inside a bare repository folder or a worktree kept inside `.git`. - Review diffs now load for a thread's out-of-tree worktree. - When a thread is bound to a worktree outside the managed folder and that folder is deleted, turn start no longer recreates it. The turn fails with the existing missing-folder error. - The handoff tool's MCP input schema no longer lists `path`. ## Testing - `apps/server` and `packages/contracts` typecheck: pass. - Targeted tests: `WorkspaceFileSystem.test.ts`, `ReviewService.test.ts`, `WorktreeMcpService.test.ts`, `ProviderTurnStartService.test.ts`: 4 files, 103 tests, all pass. - I did not run the full suite locally. CI covers the rest. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) ---
